(1) observers are able to perceive local surface shape from specular objects and that (2) object motion decreases intra-subject variability in local shape perception and (3) object motion introduces systematic differences in local shape judgments between matte and specular conditions.
(1) observers are better at judging the local shape of moving objects than of static objects, and (2) the perceived local shape of specular objects depends on the surface material.

(1) observers can use specular flow to judge local surface shape; (2) observers are more consistent when judging local surface shape of dynamic compared to static objects; and (3) observers perceive different local surface shapes when viewing dynamic matte textured and specular objects.
